newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks end modestly up after cautious session.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks end modestly up after cautious session.

text.p: Strength in banking and utility stocks allowed Hong Kong stocks to end with modest gains on Friday but the market's recent soft tone kept investors cautious and analysts said interest rates still remained a concern.
The Hang Seng Index rose 33.39 points, or 0.25 percent, to 13,321.79. Over the week it shed 57.76 points or 0.43 percent.
Turnover was HK$9.10 billion compared with HK$10.01 billion on Thursday.
"People are talking the bank sector up a little bit," said Julian Ings Chambers, assistant director at BZW Asia. Utilities had also received a boost from recent share deals, he added.
HSBC rose HK$2.00 to HK$179.50 and Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.75 to HK$91.25. But Bank of East Asia fell HK$0.90 to HK$34.90 ahead of the release of its 1996 results on Monday.
In the utilities sector, China Light continued to rise following news that CITIC Pacific would buy a 20 percent stake in the company. The stock finished at HK$36.30, up HK$0.50.
Hongkong Electric gained HK$0.80 to HK$27.55 and Hongkong Telecom added HK$0.15 to HK$13.40.
"The telecom and electric utilities saga is not over and we will see more to come. I think it is helping a bit of speculation in that part of things," said Ings Chambers.
However, analysts said the overall market looked vulnerable.
"Market turnover has been shrinking over the last few days and turnover does not show a bullish market," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at ImPac Asset Management.

He said this week's recommendation by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority that banks limit lending for luxury property acquisitions had kept property stocks under pressure and investors were worried about the direction of interest rates.
The U.S. Federal Reserve's policy-setting body meets next week. "I am not sure people are expecting much to happen," said Ings Chambers.
But he said "worries are definitely on the raising side than on the lowering side".
"You have got potentially bad news going around with U.S. interest rates and asset allocation switches away from Hong Kong into other markets that are looking a little bit cheaper," he added.
In the property sector, Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.75 to HK$87.50, Henderson Land slipped HK$0.50 to HK$71.75 and Cheung Kong fell HK$0.25 to HK$72.25.
